questions.question: Rear-view mirrors of vehicles are usually __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**convex mirrors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Convex mirrors**, also known as **diverging mirrors**, are the standard choice for **rear-view mirrors** (both side-view and interior mirrors) in **automobiles**.
 
• The primary reason for using a **convex mirror** is that it provides a much wider **field of view** compared to a **plane mirror** or a **concave mirror** because it is **curved outwards**.
 
• A **convex mirror** always forms a **virtual**, **erect**, and **diminished** image of the objects behind the vehicle, regardless of the distance of the object from the mirror.
 
• Because the images are **diminished** (smaller in size), it allows the driver to see a large area of the **traffic** behind them within a relatively small mirror surface.
 
• The **focal point** and the **center of curvature** of a **convex mirror** are imaginary points

questions.question: According to Newton’s Third Law of Motion, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Action and reaction act on the same body and are equal in magnitude.
Action and reaction are equal and opposite but act on two different bodies.
Action and reaction are unequal and act on the same body.
Action and reaction cancel each other out because they act on one body.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Action and reaction are equal and opposite but act on two different bodies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Third Law of Motion** states that whenever one object exerts a force on a second object, the second object exerts an **equal and opposite force** on the first object.
 
• According to the law, **action and reaction** are equal in **magnitude** but opposite in **direction**. They must act on **two different bodies** rather than a single body. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• If the action and reaction acted on the same body, the **net force** would always be zero, and acceleration would be impossible. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The law emphasizes that forces always occur in **pairs**; there is no such thing as an isolated single force in nature. These forces act **simultaneously** and do not result in a time lag. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Since action and reaction act on **different objects**, they do not **cancel** each other out. A force can only be canceled by another force acting on the **same object**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:** **Sir Isaac Newton** formulated the laws of motion and published them in his monumental work, **"Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica,"** in the year **1687**.
 
• **Examples of the Third Law:**
 
 
• **Recoil of a Gun:** When a bullet is fired from a **gun**, it exerts a forward force (action) on the bullet, and the bullet exerts an equal and opposite force (reaction) on the gun, causing it to **recoil**.
 
• **Walking:** When a person **walks**, they push the ground backward with their feet (action), and the **ground** pushes the person forward with an equal force (reaction).
 
• **Rocket Propulsion:** A **rocket** accelerates forward by expelling exhaust gases backward at high **velocity**; the gases exert a reaction force (thrust) on the rocket.
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Momentum:** Newton’s Third Law is the fundamental basis for the **Law of Conservation of Momentum**, which states that the total **linear momentum** of a closed system remains constant if no **external force** acts on it.
 
• **Force Definition:** In **physics**, a force is an interaction that, when unopposed, will change the **motion** of an object. It is a **vector quantity** measured in **Newtons (N)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Internal vs. External Forces:** While **action-reaction pairs** are equal and opposite, they are **internal** to the system of two interacting bodies. To change the **acceleration** of the system as a whole, an **external force** is required.
 
• **Mass and Acceleration:** Although the **magnitude** of the force is the same on both bodies, the resulting **acceleration** may differ significantly if the bodies have different **masses**, as per **Newton’s Second Law (F = ma)**. For example, the **Earth** exerts the same gravitational force on a falling **apple** as the apple exerts on the Earth, but the Earth's massive size makes its acceleration **negligible**.
</ul

questions.question: Which two physical properties allow metals to be drawn into thin wires and beaten into thin sheets, respectively?

options.text: High melting point and solid state

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ductility and malleability**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ductility** is the physical property of a material, specifically **metals**, that allows it to be stretched or drawn into **thin wires** without breaking or snapping. This property is essential for making electrical wiring.
 
• **Malleability** is the ability of a material to be deformed under **compressive stress**, which allows it to be **beaten into thin sheets** or foils using a hammer or by rolling, without cracking.
 
• Among all known elements, **Gold** is considered the most **malleable** and **ductile** metal. For instance, a **wire** of about **2 km** length can be drawn from just **1 gram** of **Gold**. ***Hence, the combination of these two properties is the correct answer.***
 
• These properties arise because the **atoms** in a **metallic lattice** are arranged in **layers** that can slide over one another when **force** is applied, while the **metallic bonds** hold the structure together.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Metallic Lustre** refers to the **shining surface** of metals in their pure state. This is due to the **reflection of light** by free electrons.
 
• **Hardness** varies from metal to metal. While **Iron** and **Copper** are hard, **alkali metals** like **Sodium** and **Potassium** are so soft that they can be cut with a **knife**.
 
 
 
• **Sonorous and Conductivity**:
 
 
• **Sonorous** metals produce a **ringing sound** when they strike a hard object. This property is used in the manufacturing of **school bells** and **musical instruments**.
 
• **Conductivity** refers to the ability to transmit **heat** and **electricity**. **Silver** is the best conductor of electricity, followed by **Copper** and **Aluminium**.
 
 
 
• **Melting Point and State**:
 
 
• Most metals are **solids** at **room temperature**, with the notable exception of **Mercury**, which is a **liquid**.
 
• Metals generally have **high melting points**. **Tungsten** has the highest melting point (about **3422°C**), making it ideal for **bulb filaments**. In contrast, **Gallium** and **Cesium** have very low melting points and can melt on a human **palm**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Nature**:
 
 
• Metals are **electropositive** elements because they lose **electrons** to form **positive ions**. When metals burn in **oxygen**, they produce **basic oxides** (like **Magnesium oxide**), whereas non-metals produce **acidic** or neutral oxides.

questions.question: What gas is typically released when ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **Ethanoic acid** (commonly known as **Acetic acid**) reacts with **Sodium carbonate** (also known as **Washing soda**), a chemical reaction occurs that releases **Carbon dioxide gas**.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is **2CH3COOH + Na2CO3 → 2CH3COONa + H2O + CO2**. In this process, **Ethanoic acid** reacts with the metal carbonate to produce **Sodium ethanoate** (a salt), **Water**, and **Carbon dioxide**.
 
• The evolution of **Carbon dioxide gas** is observed as **brisk effervescence**, which refers to the rapid formation of bubbles in the liquid as the gas escapes.
 
• This reaction is a characteristic property of **carboxylic acids**, where they react with **carbonates** and **bicarbonates** to evolve **CO2**, serving as a common laboratory test to identify the presence of a **carboxyl group**.
 
• The gas evolved can be identified by passing it through **lime water** (calcium hydroxide), which will turn **milky** due to the formation of **Calcium carbonate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ethanoic Acid (CH3COOH):**
 
 
• It is a **weak organic acid** and the second simplest **carboxylic acid** after formic acid.
 
• In its concentrated form, it is called **Glacial Acetic Acid** because it freezes at **16.6 degrees Celsius**, forming ice-like crystals.
 
• It is widely used in the food industry as **Vinegar**, which typically contains **5% to 8%** ethanoic acid by volume.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Carbonate (Na2CO3):**
 
 
• Commonly known as **Washing Soda**, it is a **basic salt** derived from a strong base and a weak acid.
 
• It is used in **glass manufacturing**, **water softening**, and as a **laboratory reagent**.
 
• When it reacts with acids, it consistently produces **Carbon dioxide**, making it useful in **fire extinguishers** and **effervescent salts**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Gas (H2):**
 
 
• Unlike carbonates, when **metals** like **Zinc** or **Magnesium** react with acids, they typically release **Hydrogen gas**.
 
• **Hydrogen** is a colorless, odorless gas that burns with a **pop sound** when a burning splinter is brought near it.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen Gas (O2):**
 
 
• **Oxygen** is not typically released in simple acid-base neutralization or acid-carbonate reactions.
 
• It is usually produced during the **decomposition** of certain oxides or **electrolysis of water**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reaction with Sodium Bicarbonate:** **Ethanoic acid** also reacts with **Sodium bicarbonate** (**NaHCO3**, or baking soda) to produce the same gas, **Carbon dioxide**. The equation is **CH3COOH + NaHCO3 → CH3COONa + H2O + CO2**.
 
• **Test for Carbon Dioxide:** To confirm the identity of the gas, it is passed through **Lime Water** [**Ca(OH)2**]. The lime water turns **milky** because of the formation of insoluble **Calcium Carbonate** (**CaCO3**). If the gas is passed in excess, the milkiness disappears due to the formation of soluble **Calcium Hydrogen Carbonate** [**Ca(HCO3)2**].
 
• **Functional Group Identification:** The reaction with **Sodium Carbonate** is a standard **analytical test** to distinguish **carboxylic acids** from **phenols** and **alcohols**, as the latter do not typically release **CO2** with carbonates.
 
• **Salt Formation:** The salt formed in this specific reaction, **Sodium ethanoate** (**CH3COONa**), is used in the **textile industry** and as a **buffering agent** in various chemical applications.
</ul

questions.question: Name the scientist who defined elements as substances that CANNOT be broken down into simpler form by chemical reactions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Antoine Laurent Lavoisier**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Antoine Laurent Lavoisier** (1743–1794) was a prominent **French chemist** who is widely regarded as the "**Father of Modern Chemistry**" for his revolutionary contributions to the field.
 
• He was the first scientist to establish a strictly functional and modern definition of a chemical **element**.
 
• **Lavoisier** defined an **element** as a basic form of matter that **cannot be broken down** into simpler substances by any known **chemical reaction**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• His findings and this specific definition were published in his landmark book, **Traité Élémentaire de Chimie** (Elementary Treatise on Chemistry), in the year **1789**.
 
• In this work, he listed **33 substances** that he considered elements based on this definition, including **oxygen**, **nitrogen**, **hydrogen**, **phosphorus**, **mercury**, **zinc**, and **sulfur**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Robert Boyle:**
 
 
• **Robert Boyle** was an **Anglo-Irish** natural philosopher and chemist.
 
• In **1661**, in his book **The Sceptical Chymist**, he was the first to use the term "**element**" in a scientific context to challenge the ancient Greek idea of four elements (earth, air, fire, water).
 
• While he laid the conceptual groundwork, he did not provide the experimental definition that **Lavoisier** later perfected.
 
 
 
• **Robert Hooke:**
 
 
• **Robert Hooke** (often misspelled as Hookie) was an **English** polymath and architect.
 
• He is most famous for discovering the law of elasticity, known as **Hooke's Law**, and for his work in microscopy.
 
• In **1665**, he published **Micrographia**, where he used a microscope to observe cork and coined the biological term "**cell**."
 
 
 
• **Charles Darwin:**
 
 
• **Charles Darwin** was an **English** naturalist, geologist, and biologist.
 
• He is best known for his contributions to the **science of evolution**.
 
• His theory of **natural selection** was detailed in his **1859** book, **On the Origin of Species**, which transformed the biological sciences.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass:** **Lavoisier** formulated this fundamental law, which states that in a chemical reaction, the **mass** of the products is always equal to the mass of the reactants; **matter** is neither created nor destroyed.
 
• **Oxygen and Combustion:** He played a vital role in naming **oxygen** in **1778** and **hydrogen** in **1783**. He effectively debunked the **phlogiston theory** by proving that **oxygen** is necessary for combustion to occur.
 
• **Chemical Nomenclature:** Along with other colleagues, **Lavoisier** helped devise the first systematic method of **chemical nomenclature**, ensuring that the name of a chemical compound reflects its elemental composition.
 
• **Metric System:** As a member of various French academies, he was instrumental in the development of the **metric system** to standardize weights and measures across **France**.

questions.question: A force (F) of 60 N acts on a mass (m) of 6 kg. What will be the acceleration (a) produced by this force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10.0 m/s2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between the applied force, the mass of an object, and the resulting acceleration is defined by **Newton’s Second Law of Motion**.
 
• According to this law, the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass. The mathematical formula is expressed as **F = m × a**, or **a = F / m**.
 
• In the given problem, the **Force (F)** acting on the object is **60 N** and the **Mass (m)** of the object is **6 kg**.
 
• By substituting these values into the acceleration formula: **a = 60 N / 6 kg**.
 
• The calculation results in an **acceleration (a)** of **10.0 m/s2**. ***Hence, the calculated value matches the correct option.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton (N)**: It is the **SI unit of force**. One Newton is defined as the amount of force required to give a mass of **1 kilogram** an acceleration of **1 meter per second squared** (1 kg·m/s2).
 
• **Mass (m)**: This is a fundamental property of matter that represents an object's resistance to acceleration when a force is applied. It is a **scalar quantity** and is measured in **kilograms (kg)** in the **SI system**.
 
• **Acceleration (a)**: This is a **vector quantity** that describes the rate at which an object changes its velocity. Its standard unit is **meters per second squared (m/s2)**.
 
• **Newton's Second Law**: This law states that the **acceleration** of an object as produced by a net force is directly proportional to the magnitude of the net force, in the same direction as the net force, and inversely proportional to the mass of the object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vector Nature**: Since **Force** is a vector, the **acceleration** produced will always occur in the **same direction** as the applied net force.
 
• **Inertia**: Mass is a measure of **inertia**; therefore, a larger mass requires a greater force to achieve the same acceleration as a smaller mass.
 
• **Dimensional Consistency**: When performing physics calculations, it is vital to ensure units are consistent. If the force is in **Newtons** and mass is in **kilograms**, the acceleration will naturally result in **m/s2**.
 
• **Zero Acceleration**: If the net force acting on a mass is **zero**, the acceleration will also be **zero**, meaning the object will either remain at rest or continue to move at a **constant velocity**, as per **Newton's First Law**.

questions.question: The symbol of an element represents which of the following?

options.text: The full name of the element
One atom of the element only

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One atom of the element only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **symbol of an element** is a shorthand notation or abbreviation used in chemistry to represent a specific chemical element. Primarily, it represents **one atom** of that element in a chemical reaction or formula. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• A chemical symbol provides a **qualitative** and **quantitative** representation. Qualitatively, it identifies the name of the element; quantitatively, it represents **one atom** or a **definite mass** (atomic mass) of that element.
 
• While the symbol is derived from the name, it is not the **full name** itself but a standardized abbreviation consisting of one or two letters. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The concept of **one mole** of an element refers to **6.022 x 10²³ atoms** (Avogadro's number). While a symbol in a balanced chemical equation can represent a molar ratio, fundamentally, the symbol itself stands for a single atomic unit. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **atomic number** (number of protons) and **mass number** (protons plus neutrons) are numerical properties of an atom. Although they are often written alongside a symbol (as subscript and superscript), the symbol itself does not inherently "represent" these numbers; it represents the identity of the element. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• For example, the symbol **"C"** represents **one atom of Carbon**. Similarly, **"He"** represents **one atom of Helium**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin of Chemical Symbols:** The modern system of using letters to represent elements was proposed by the Swedish chemist **J.J. Berzelius** in the early **19th century** (specifically around **1813**). Before this, alchemists used complex pictorial symbols.
 
• **Naming Conventions:** The first letter of a symbol is always **capitalized**, while the second letter (if present) is always **lowercase**. For instance, **Co** represents **Cobalt**, whereas **CO** represents **Carbon Monoxide** (a compound).
 
• **Latin and Greek Roots:** Many symbols are derived from the **Latin** or **Greek** names of elements. For example, **Fe** comes from **Ferrum** (Iron), **Au** from **Aurum** (Gold), **Cu** from **Cuprum** (Copper), and **Na** from **Natrium** (Sodium).
 
• **IUPAC Standardization:** The **International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC)** is the global authority that approves the official names and symbols for newly discovered elements to ensure consistency in scientific communication across all **countries**.
 
• **Significance in Formulas:** When a subscript is added to a symbol, it indicates the number of atoms in a molecule. For example, **H** represents **one atom of Hydrogen**, but **H₂** represents **one molecule of Hydrogen** consisting of two atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Atomic Mass Unit (amu):** The symbol of an element also represents a mass equal to its **atomic mass** expressed in **atomic mass units**. For example, the symbol **O** represents **16 amu** of Oxygen.
 
• **Gram Atomic Mass:** In laboratory calculations, the symbol can represent the **gram atomic mass** of an element, which is the mass of one mole of atoms in grams.
 
• **Valency:** The symbol is used to determine the **valency** or combining capacity of an element when writing chemical formulas using the **criss-cross method**.
 
• **Isotopes:** Symbols are also used to distinguish between **isotopes** of the same element by adding the mass number, such as **¹²C** and **¹⁴C**, though the base symbol remains the same as the number of **protons** (atomic number) does not change.
</ul

questions.question: Carbohydrates produced in photosynthesis but not immediately used are stored as ________ in plants.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**starch**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the process of **photosynthesis**, plants utilize **sunlight**, **water**, and **carbon dioxide** to produce **glucose**, which serves as their primary source of energy.
 
• **Glucose** is a simple sugar (**monosaccharide**) that is highly **soluble** in water; if stored directly, it would increase the **osmotic pressure** within the plant cells, potentially causing them to burst or lose water balance.
 
• To prevent this, plants convert the surplus **glucose** into **starch**, a complex **polysaccharide**. **Starch** is **insoluble** in water and chemically **inert**, making it the most efficient form for long-term **energy storage**.
 
• This **starch** is stored in various parts of the plant, including the **chloroplasts** of leaves and specialized organelles called **amyloplasts** located in **roots**, **seeds**, and **tubers**.
 
• When the plant requires energy during periods without sunlight, such as at **night** or during **dormancy**, it breaks down the stored **starch** back into **glucose** to fuel its metabolic activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Glucose:** It is the **immediate product** of **photosynthesis**. It provides the energy needed for **cellular respiration** and acts as a building block for other organic molecules. However, it is not the primary storage molecule.
 
• **Cellulose:** While also a polymer of **glucose**, **cellulose** is a **structural carbohydrate**. It is the main component of the plant **cell wall**, providing **rigidity** and **mechanical strength**. Unlike **starch**, it is not used as a reserve food source.
 
• **Proteins:** These are **macromolecules** made of **amino acids**. Plants synthesize **proteins** by combining the **carbohydrates** produced in **photosynthesis** with **nitrogen**, **phosphorus**, and **sulfur** absorbed from the **soil**. They are essential for **growth** and **enzymatic functions**.
 
• **Sucrose:** This is a **disaccharide** (composed of **glucose** and **fructose**). **Sucrose** is the form in which **carbohydrates** are **transported** or **translocated** through the **phloem** from the leaves to other parts of the plant like the **roots** and **fruits**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Composition of Starch:** Starch is composed of two types of **glucose polymers**: **amylose** (a linear chain) and **amylopectin** (a highly branched chain).
 
• **Iodine Test:** The presence of **starch** in a plant leaf can be confirmed using the **Iodine Test**. When **iodine solution** is added to a leaf containing starch, it turns **blue-black** in color.
 
• **Animal Storage:** It is important to note that while plants store **carbohydrates** as **starch**, animals (including humans) store their excess **glucose** as **glycogen** in the **liver** and **muscles**.
 
• **Economic Importance:** Many **staple foods** consumed by humans, such as **potatoes**, **rice**, **wheat**, and **maize**, are rich in **starch** because these plants store significant reserves in their **tubers** or **grains**.
 
• **Conversion Process:** The conversion of **glucose** to **starch** involves a series of **enzymatic reactions**, specifically during the **Calvin cycle** and subsequent metabolic pathways in the **stroma** of the **chloroplast**.
</ul

questions.question: The magnetic field is strongest:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**near the conductor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **magnetic field strength** (magnetic flux density) produced by a **straight current-carrying conductor** is directly proportional to the **magnitude of the current** and inversely proportional to the **distance** from the conductor.
 
• According to **Ampere’s Circuital Law** and the **Biot-Savart Law**, the magnetic field (**B**) at a point is given by the relation **B ∝ 1/r**, where **r** is the radial distance from the wire.
 
• **Near the conductor**: As the distance **r** decreases, the value of the magnetic field **B** increases significantly. Therefore, the field is at its maximum intensity in the immediate proximity of the wire. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Far from the conductor**: As the distance **r** increases, the magnetic field strength weakens rapidly. At very large distances, the field becomes negligible. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Outside a solenoid**: In an ideal **solenoid**, the magnetic field lines are nearly parallel and very close together inside, but they spread out extensively in the exterior space. The magnetic field **outside a solenoid** is considered to be **zero** or extremely weak. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Equidistant from the conductor**: Points that are equidistant from the conductor lie on a **concentric circle**. While the magnetic field strength is **uniform** (the same) at all these points, this phrase does not describe where the field is "strongest" relative to other locations. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right-Hand Thumb Rule**:

 
 
• This rule is used to determine the **direction** of the magnetic field around a straight conductor.
 
• If you hold the conductor in your **right hand** such that the **thumb** points in the direction of the **electric current**, then your **fingers** will curl around the conductor in the direction of the **magnetic field lines**.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Magnetic Field Lines**:
 
 
• For a straight wire, the field lines form **concentric circles** centered on the wire.
 
• The **density** of these field lines indicates the strength; they are crowded **near the conductor** and become spaced out as we move away.
 
• Magnetic field lines **never intersect** each other.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field in a Solenoid**:
 
 
• A **solenoid** is a long coil containing a large number of close turns of **insulated copper wire**.
 
• The magnetic field **inside** a solenoid is **uniform** and strong, represented by parallel straight lines. This property is used to magnetize materials like **soft iron** to create **electromagnets**.
 
 
 
• **Units and Discovery**:
 
 
• The **SI unit** of magnetic field strength is the **Tesla (T)**, named after the physicist **Nikola Tesla**.
 
• In **1820**, **Hans Christian Oersted** discovered that an electric current creates a magnetic field, marking the birth of **electromagnetism**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Factors affecting the Magnetic Field**:

 
 
• **Current (I)**: Increasing the current increases the magnetic field strength (**B ∝ I**).
 
• **Number of Turns (N)**: In a coil or solenoid, the field is proportional to the number of turns (**B ∝ N**).
 
• **Medium**: The presence of a **ferromagnetic core** (like soft iron) inside a coil increases the magnetic field intensity by thousands of times due to high **magnetic permeability**.
 
 
 
• **Mathematical Representation**: For an infinitely long straight wire, the formula is **B = (μ₀I) / (2πr)**, where **μ₀** is the **permeability of free space** (approximately **4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A**).

questions.question: The twinkling of stars is more pronounced when _______.

options.text: the star is at the zenith
the star is near the horizon

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the star is near the horizon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **twinkling of stars**, scientifically known as **stellar scintillation**, is caused by the **atmospheric refraction** of starlight as it passes through the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• When a star is **near the horizon**, the light coming from it has to travel through a **much thicker layer of the atmosphere** compared to when it is directly overhead (at the **zenith**).
 
• Because the light travels through more **atmospheric layers** with varying **densities** and **temperatures**, it undergoes multiple refractions. These layers are constantly moving due to **thermal turbulence** and **wind**, causing the light to bend in different directions rapidly.
 
• This continuous change in the **refractive index** of the air causes the **apparent position** and **brightness** of the star to fluctuate, making the twinkling effect more visible and pronounced. ***Hence, the correct answer is the star is near the horizon.***
 
• In contrast, when a star is at the **zenith**, the starlight enters the atmosphere **perpendicularly** and travels the **shortest distance**, resulting in minimal refraction and less twinkling. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atmospheric Refraction:** This phenomenon occurs because the **Earth's atmosphere** is not uniform. It consists of several layers with different **optical densities**. As starlight enters the atmosphere, it gradually bends towards the **normal** because the air becomes denser closer to the Earth's surface.
 
• **Planets do not twinkle:** Unlike stars, which act as **point sources** of light due to their immense distance, **planets** are much closer to Earth and are seen as **extended sources** (a collection of many point sources). While the individual points of light from a planet may twinkle, the **average brightness** remains constant as the fluctuations cancel each other out.
 
• **Apparent Position:** Due to **refraction**, a star appears slightly **higher** in the sky than its **actual position**. This effect is most significant when the star is near the **horizon**.
 
• **Sky conditions:** While a **cloudy sky** might block starlight entirely or scatter it, it does not specifically make the "twinkling" more pronounced in a scientific sense; rather, it often obscures the star. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Moonlight:** A **bright moon** increases the background **luminance** of the sky, which can actually make it harder to observe the subtle intensity changes of twinkling stars. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Refractive Index:** The **refractive index** of air depends on its **temperature**. Hot air is less dense and has a lower refractive index than cold air. The mixing of these air masses creates **turbulent cells** that act like tiny moving **lenses**.
 
• **Vacuum:** If there were no **atmosphere** (such as on the **Moon** or in **outer space**), stars would appear as steady, non-twinkling points of light because there would be no medium to refract the light.
 
• **Color Flashing:** Very bright stars near the **horizon** (like **Sirius**) often appear to flash different **colors**. This is because the atmosphere acts as a **prism**, dispersing the white starlight into its component colors through **chromatic refraction**.
 
• **Observation:** Astronomers often place **telescopes** on **high mountains** or in **space** (like the **Hubble Space Telescope**) to avoid the "blurring" and "twinkling" caused by the Earth's **turbulent atmosphere**, allowing for clearer images.
</ul

questions.question: What is the primary function of the kidneys in human beings?

options.text: To filter nitrogenous waste materials from the blood
To regulate digestion and nutrient absorption
To absorb oxygen and release carbon dioxide
To transport glucose and hormones throughout the body

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To filter nitrogenous waste materials from the blood**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **kidneys** are the primary organs of the human **excretory system**, responsible for maintaining the chemical balance of the body by processing **blood**.
 
• Their most critical function is to filter out metabolic waste products, specifically **nitrogenous wastes** such as **urea**, **uric acid**, and **creatinine**, from the **bloodstream**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• Each kidney contains approximately **1 million** structural and functional units called **nephrons**, which perform the actual filtration process.
 
• The filtration process in the **nephron** involves **glomerular filtration** (ultrafiltration), **tubular reabsorption**, and **tubular secretion** to ensure essential nutrients are retained while wastes are removed.
 
• The waste product formed after this filtration process is **urine**, which is then excreted from the body through the **ureters**, **urinary bladder**, and **urethra**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Homeostasis and Osmoregulation**: The kidneys play a vital role in maintaining **homeostasis** by regulating the **osmolarity** of body fluids. They control the levels of **water** and **electrolytes** like **sodium**, **potassium**, and **calcium**.
 
• **Regulation of Blood Pressure**: Through the **Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS)**, the kidneys help regulate long-term **blood pressure** by adjusting blood volume and vascular resistance.
 
• **Endocrine Functions**: The kidneys act as endocrine organs by secreting hormones such as **Erythropoietin**, which stimulates the production of **red blood cells** in the **bone marrow**, and **Renin**.
 
• **Vitamin D Activation**: They are responsible for converting **calcifediol** into **calcitriol**, the active form of **Vitamin D**, which is essential for **calcium** absorption in the intestines.
 
• **pH Balance**: The kidneys help maintain the **acid-base balance** (pH) of the **blood** by excreting hydrogen ions and reabsorbing bicarbonate from the urine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Anatomy**: In a healthy adult, each kidney is about **10-12 cm** long, **5-7 cm** wide, and weighs approximately **120-170 grams**. They are located in the **retroperitoneal space** at the level of **T12 to L3 vertebrae**.
 
• **Filtration Rate**: The kidneys filter about **180 liters** of fluid daily; however, nearly **99%** of this is reabsorbed into the **blood**, resulting in only about **1.5 liters** of **urine** production per day.
 
• **Comparison with Other Functions**:
 
 
• **Digestion and nutrient absorption** (Option 2) are primarily the functions of the **stomach** and **small intestine**.
 
• **Oxygen absorption and carbon dioxide release** (Option 3) are the primary functions of the **lungs** in the **respiratory system**.
 
• **Transport of glucose and hormones** (Option 4) is handled by the **circulatory system** (heart and blood vessels).
 
 
 
• **Renal Failure**: When kidneys lose their ability to filter, it leads to a condition called **uremia**, which may require medical interventions like **dialysis** or a **kidney transplant**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following contraceptive devices is placed in the uterus to prevent pregnancy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper-T**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Copper-T (CuT)** is a type of **Intrauterine Device (IUD)** that is inserted by medical professionals or expert nurses into the **uterus** through the **vagina**.
 
• It is a **non-hormonal** contraceptive device made of plastic and **copper**. It is **T-shaped** to fit the anatomy of the uterine cavity.
 
• The primary mechanism of action involves the release of **copper ions**, which increase the **phagocytosis of sperm** within the **uterus**.
 
• The released **copper ions** also suppress **sperm motility** and reduce the **fertilizing capacity** of the sperm, thereby preventing the sperm from reaching and fertilizing the egg.
 
• It is considered one of the most effective **long-term** reversible contraceptive methods, with specific models like **CuT-380A** providing protection for up to **10 years**.
 
• In **India**, IUDs like **Copper-T** are widely accepted as a primary method of contraception for women who wish to **space children** or delay pregnancy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Condom**:
 
 
• It is a **barrier method** of contraception made of thin rubber or **latex sheath**.
 
• It is used to cover the **penis** in the male or the **vagina and cervix** in the female just before coitus.
 
• Unlike IUDs, condoms prevent the **physical meeting** of the sperm and the ovum and offer the added benefit of protecting against **Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)** and **AIDS**.
 
 
 
• **Oral Pills**:
 
 
• These are **hormonal contraceptives** taken in the form of tablets. They contain small doses of either **progestogens** or a **progestogen-estrogen combination**.
 
• They work by inhibiting **ovulation** and **implantation**, as well as altering the quality of **cervical mucus** to prevent/retard the entry of sperm.
 
• **Saheli** is a well-known **non-steroidal** oral pill developed by the **Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI)** in **Lucknow**, India.
 
 
 
• **Hormonal Patch**:
 
 
• This is a **transdermal patch** applied to the skin that releases **synthetic estrogen and progestogen** hormones into the bloodstream.
 
• Similar to oral pills, the patch prevents **ovulation** (the release of an egg from the ovary) and thickens the **cervical mucus**.
 
 
 
• **Categories of IUDs**:
 
 
• **Non-medicated IUDs**: Example includes the **Lippes Loop**.
 
• **Copper releasing IUDs**: Examples include **CuT, Cu7, and Multiload 375**.
 
• **Hormone releasing IUDs**: Examples include **Progestasert and LNG-20**, which make the uterus unsuitable for **implantation** and the cervix hostile to sperm.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **effectiveness** of **Copper-T** starts immediately upon insertion by a healthcare provider.
 
• While **Copper-T** is highly effective at preventing **pregnancy**, it does **not** provide any protection against **HIV/AIDS** or other **sexually transmitted diseases**.
 
• It is a **reversible** method; fertility returns to normal as soon as the device is removed from the **uterus**.
 
• Common side effects may include **heavier menstrual bleeding** or cramping, especially in the first few **months** after insertion.
</ul

questions.question: What type of chemical bond is typically formed when a metal reacts with a non-metal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ionic bond**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **Ionic bond** is a type of chemical linkage formed through the **electrostatic attraction** between two oppositely charged ions. This bond typically forms when a **metal** reacts with a **non-metal**.
 
• During the formation of an ionic bond, the **metal atom** loses one or more **valence electrons** to become a positively charged ion, known as a **cation**.
 
• The **non-metal atom** accepts these electrons to complete its outer shell, becoming a negatively charged ion, known as an **anion**.
 
• This **complete transfer of electrons** happens because metals generally have **low ionization energy** (they lose electrons easily), while non-metals have **high electron affinity** (they gain electrons easily).
 
• A common example is **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, where a **Sodium (Na)** atom (metal) transfers its single valence electron to a **Chlorine (Cl)** atom (non-metal). ***Hence, the correct answer is Ionic bond.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Covalent Bond:**
 
 
• This bond involves the **sharing of electron pairs** between atoms. It typically occurs between two **non-metals**.
 
• Examples include **Water (H₂O)**, **Methane (CH₄)**, and **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)**.
 
• Unlike ionic bonds, there is no complete transfer of electrons; instead, the atoms reach stability by sharing.
 
 
 
• **Metallic Bond:**
 
 
• This bond occurs specifically between **metal atoms**. It is characterized by a "**sea of delocalized electrons**" that move freely around a lattice of positive metal nuclei.
 
• This structure accounts for properties like **electrical conductivity**, **malleability**, and **ductility** in metals like **Copper (Cu)** and **Iron (Fe)**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Bond:**
 
 
• This is a relatively weak **intermolecular force** rather than a primary chemical bond.
 
• It occurs when a **hydrogen atom** is covalently bonded to a highly **electronegative atom** (such as **Nitrogen**, **Oxygen**, or **Fluorine**) and experiences attraction to another electronegative atom nearby.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Electronegativity Difference:** The nature of a bond is often determined by the **electronegativity** difference between the two elements. If the difference is greater than **1.7** on the Pauling scale, the bond is usually **Ionic**; if it is lower, it is **Covalent**.
 
• **Physical State:** Ionic compounds are typically **crystalline solids** at **room temperature** and have very **high melting and boiling points** due to the strong attraction between ions.
 
• **Conductivity:** Ionic compounds do not conduct electricity in **solid form** because the ions are fixed in place. However, they are **excellent conductors** when **molten** or **dissolved in water** (aqueous state) because the ions are free to move.
 
• **Lattice Energy:** The stability of an ionic compound is derived from its **lattice energy**, which is the energy released when gaseous ions combine to form a solid ionic crystal.
 
• **Octet Rule:** The primary driving force for forming ionic bonds is the **Octet Rule**, where atoms lose or gain electrons to achieve a stable electronic configuration similar to **Noble Gases** (usually **8 electrons** in the outermost shell).

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct sequence in extraction of metals from ore?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concentration → Reduction → Refining**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The extraction of metals from their ores involves several physical and chemical processes collectively known as **Metallurgy**. The standard sequence followed is **Concentration**, followed by **Reduction**, and finally **Refining**.
 
• **Concentration of Ore**: Also known as **ore-dressing** or **beneficiation**, this is the initial step where impurities such as **sand**, **clay**, and **rocks** (collectively called **gangue**) are removed from the mined ore. Methods used include **hydraulic washing**, **magnetic separation**, or **froth flotation**. ***Hence, the first stage in the sequence is Concentration.***
 
• **Reduction**: Once the ore is concentrated and usually converted into a **metal oxide** (via **roasting** or **calcination**), it undergoes reduction. In this stage, the metal oxide is reduced to the **crude metal** by removing oxygen. This is often done using reducing agents like **carbon (coke)**, **carbon monoxide**, or through **electrolysis** for highly reactive metals. ***Hence, the second stage in the sequence is Reduction.***
 
• **Refining**: The metal obtained after reduction is usually **impure** and contains other metals or non-metals. Refining is the final treatment to obtain **pure metal** of high grade. Common techniques include **distillation**, **liquation**, and **electrolytic refining**. ***Hence, the third stage in the sequence is Refining.***
 
• Therefore, the correct operational sequence in metallurgical extraction is **Concentration → Reduction → Refining**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gangue and Flux**: **Gangue** refers to the earthy impurities associated with the ore. A substance called **Flux** is added during the extraction process to remove gangue by forming a fusible material known as **Slag**.
 
• **Roasting and Calcination**:
 
 
• **Roasting**: The process of heating **sulphide ores** strongly in the **presence of excess air** to convert them into oxides.
 
• **Calcination**: The process of heating **carbonate or hydrated ores** strongly in the **absence or limited supply of air** to remove volatile impurities and convert them into oxides.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity Series and Extraction**:
 
 
• **High Reactivity Metals** (e.g., **Sodium**, **Magnesium**, **Aluminium**): These are extracted by **electrolytic reduction** of their molten chlorides or oxides because they cannot be reduced by carbon.
 
• **Medium Reactivity Metals** (e.g., **Zinc**, **Iron**, **Lead**): Usually found as sulphides or carbonates, converted to oxides, and then reduced using **carbon**.
 
• **Low Reactivity Metals** (e.g., **Mercury**, **Copper**): These can often be reduced to metal by simply heating their ores in air.
 
 
 
• **Electrolytic Refining**: This is the most widely used method for refining metals like **Copper (Cu)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, and **Nickel (Ni)**. In this process, the **impure metal** acts as the **anode**, and a thin strip of **pure metal** acts as the **cathode**. On passing electricity, pure metal from the anode dissolves into the electrolyte and deposits onto the cathode.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Froth Flotation**: This specific concentration method is primarily used for **sulphide ores**. It relies on the principle that ore particles are wetted by **oil** while gangue particles are wetted by **water**.
 
• **Thermite Process**: A reduction method where a **highly reactive metal** like **Aluminium** is used as a reducing agent to displace a metal from its oxide, often used for joining railway tracks (**Iron oxide** reduction).
 
• **Purity Levels**: While concentration increases the percentage of the metal in the ore, and reduction yields the metal, only **Refining** ensures a purity level often exceeding **99.9%**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about sound propagation is true?

options.text: Sound is the fastest in gases, slower in liquids and the slowest in solids.
Sound is the fastest in solids, slower in liquids and the slowest in gases.
Sound can travel in a vacuum.
Sound travels at the same speed in all mediums.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sound is the fastest in solids, slower in liquids and the slowest in gases.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sound** is a **mechanical wave** that requires a **material medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel. It cannot travel through a vacuum.
 
• The speed of sound depends on the **elasticity** and **density** of the medium. In **solids**, the molecules are **tightly packed** and held together by strong **intermolecular forces**, allowing vibrations to transfer very rapidly. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• In **liquids**, the molecules are less tightly packed than in solids but more so than in gases. Consequently, sound travels **slower in liquids** than in solids but **faster than in gases**. For example, the speed of sound in **water** is approximately **1480 m/s**.
 
• In **gases**, molecules are far apart, meaning the collisions between them occur less frequently, which results in the **slowest speed of propagation**. For instance, in **air** at **20°C**, sound travels at approximately **343 m/s**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Sound cannot travel through a **vacuum** because there are no particles to carry the vibrations. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The speed of sound is **not the same** in all mediums; it varies significantly based on the **physical state** and **temperature** of the substance. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Sound Waves**: 
 
 
• Sound waves are **longitudinal waves**, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate **parallel** to the direction of the wave's propagation.
 
• In solids, sound can also travel as **transverse waves**, but in fluids (liquids and gases), they are primarily longitudinal.
 
 
 
• **Effect of Temperature**:
 
 
• The speed of sound **increases** with an increase in **temperature**. For example, in air, the speed increases by approximately **0.6 meters per second** for every **1 degree Celsius** rise in temperature.
 
• This happens because higher temperatures increase the **kinetic energy** of the molecules, leading to more frequent collisions.
 
 
 
• **Elasticity vs. Density**:
 
 
• While higher **density** usually tends to slow down sound, the significantly higher **elasticity** (bulk modulus) of solids more than compensates for their density, resulting in the **highest speeds** in materials like **steel** (approx **5960 m/s**) or **aluminum** (approx **6420 m/s**).
 
 
 
• **Historical Context and Applications**:
 
 
• The **Bell Jar Experiment** is a classic scientific demonstration used to prove that sound cannot travel in a **vacuum**.
 
• Understanding sound propagation is essential in fields like **SONAR** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) used by **submarines**, medical **ultrasonography**, and **seismology** to study **Earth's interior**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Human Hearing Range**: The human ear can typically hear frequencies between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz (20 kHz)**.
 
• **Infrasonic and Ultrasonic**: Sounds with frequencies below **20 Hz** are called **infrasonic** (often produced by **elephants** or **whales**), while frequencies above **20,000 Hz** are **ultrasonic** (used by **bats** for navigation).
 
• **Mach Number**: This is the ratio of the speed of an object to the speed of sound in the surrounding medium. If an aircraft travels faster than sound, it is called **supersonic**, which produces a **sonic boom**.

questions.question: Which of the following enzymes is present in saliva?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salivary Amylase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Salivary amylase**, also referred to as **ptyalin**, is the primary enzyme present in the **saliva** of humans and several other mammals.
 
• It is synthesized and secreted by the **salivary glands**, which include the **parotid**, **submandibular**, and **sublingual** glands.
 
• The main function of this enzyme is to initiate the **chemical digestion** of **carbohydrates** (specifically starch) in the **buccal cavity** (mouth).
 
• **Salivary amylase** works by breaking down the long chains of **starch** (polysaccharides) into simpler disaccharides like **maltose** and smaller polymers called **dextrins**.
 
• The enzyme operates most efficiently at an **optimum pH of 6.8**, which is slightly acidic, and requires **chloride ions (Cl-)** for its activation.
 
• It is estimated that nearly **30 percent** of the total dietary **starch** is hydrolyzed in the oral cavity before the food reaches the stomach. ***Hence, the correct answer is Salivary Amylase.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Composition of Saliva:**
 
 
• Saliva is a watery fluid containing 99.5% water and 0.5% solutes, including **electrolytes** like **Sodium (Na+)**, **Potassium (K+)**, **Chloride (Cl-)**, and **Bicarbonate (HCO3-)**.

• According to **Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation**, every particle attracts every other particle in the universe with a force that is **directly proportional** to the product of their **masses** and **inversely proportional** to the **square of the distance** between their centers.
 
• The mathematical expression for this force is **F = G (M × m) / r²**, where **G** is the **Gravitational Constant**, **M** is the mass of the **Earth**, **m** is the mass of the **body**, and **r** is the distance between them.

• By rearranging the equation, we get **F' = 4 × [G (M × m) / r²]**. Since the term in the bracket is the original force **F**, the new force becomes **4F**. ***Hence, the gravitational force increases by four times.***

• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g):** On the surface of the Earth, the value of **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. It is derived from the formula **g = GM / r²**, showing that the acceleration of a falling object does not depend on the **mass of the object** itself, but the force acting on it does.

questions.question: In a schematic electric circuit diagram, how is a voltmeter typically represented when connected to measure potential difference?

options.text: A circle with a ‘V’ inside, connected in parallel
A square with a ‘V’ inside, connected in parallel
A circle with an ‘A’ inside, connected in series
A rectangle with an ‘R’ inside, connected in series

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A circle with a ‘V’ inside, connected in parallel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **schematic electric circuit diagram**, a **voltmeter** is represented by a **circle with the letter ‘V’** inscribed inside it. This device is specifically designed to measure the **electric potential difference** between two points in a circuit.
 
• A **voltmeter** must always be connected in **parallel** with the component or part of the circuit across which the voltage is to be measured. This is because the potential difference remains the same across all branches in a parallel connection. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The standard symbol for a voltmeter is a circle; using a **square with a ‘V’** is not a standard practice in conventional electrical schematics. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• A **circle with an ‘A’** inside represents an **ammeter**, which is used to measure **electric current**. Unlike a voltmeter, an ammeter is connected in **series** because current remains constant in a series circuit. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• A **rectangle with an ‘R’** (or more commonly a **zig-zag line**) represents a **resistor**, which is a passive component that provides **resistance** to the flow of current, rather than a measuring instrument. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• An **ideal voltmeter** is considered to have **infinite resistance**. This characteristic ensures that it does not draw any significant current from the main circuit, thereby providing an accurate reading of the potential difference without altering the circuit's behavior.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Potential Difference (Voltage):**
 
 
• It is defined as the **work done** to move a **unit positive charge** from one point to another in an electric field. The **SI unit** of potential difference is the **Volt (V)**, named after the physicist **Alessandro Volta**.
 
• Mathematically, **Voltage (V) = Work Done (W) / Charge (Q)**.
 
 
 
• **Ammeter vs. Voltmeter:**
 
 
• An **ammeter** measures current in **Amperes (A)** and has **very low resistance** to minimize its impact on the total circuit resistance. It is always placed in **series**.
 
• A **voltmeter** measures voltage in **Volts (V)** and has **very high resistance**. It is always placed in **parallel**.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Proposed by **Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, it states that the current passing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, provided physical conditions like temperature remain constant (**V = IR**).
 
 
 
• **Galvanometer:**
 
 
• A **galvanometer** is an instrument used for detecting and measuring **small electric currents**. It can be converted into a voltmeter by connecting a **high resistance (multiplier) in series** with it.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Circuit Safety:** Connecting a voltmeter in series can stop the flow of current in a circuit due to its **exceptionally high resistance**, rendering the circuit non-functional. Conversely, connecting an ammeter in parallel can lead to a **short circuit** and damage the meter because of its low resistance.
 
• **Measurement Units:**
 
 
• **1 Volt** is the potential difference between two points when **1 Joule** of work is done to move a charge of **1 Coulomb**.
 
• Instruments like the **Multimeter** are versatile tools that can function as a voltmeter, ammeter, or ohmmeter depending on the setting chosen by the user.
 
 
 
• **Schematic Symbols:** Standard symbols facilitate global communication among engineers. A **battery** is shown as a series of long and short parallel lines, while a **switch** is shown as a break in the line that can be "opened" or "closed."

questions.question: Which of the following is a colloidal solution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Milk**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Milk** is considered a **colloidal solution** because it consists of **liquid fat globules** dispersed throughout an **aqueous (water-based) solution**.
 
• A **colloid** is a **heterogeneous mixture** in which the particle size of the substance is intermediate between a **true solution** and a **suspension**. The diameter of the particles typically ranges from **1 nanometer to 1000 nanometers**.
 
• In **milk**, the **dispersed phase** is **fat (lipids)** and the **dispersion medium** is **water**. Because both the dispersed phase and the medium are liquids, it is specifically categorized as an **emulsion**.
 
• Colloids like **milk** exhibit the **Tyndall effect**, which is the **scattering of a beam of light** as it passes through the mixture, making the path of light visible.
 
• Unlike **suspensions**, the particles in a **colloidal solution** do not settle down at the bottom when left undisturbed for a long period, showing that **milk** is relatively **stable**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Salt Water**: 
 
 
• It is a **True Solution**. In this mixture, the **sodium chloride (NaCl)** particles are completely dissolved in **water**.
 
• The **particle size** is less than **1 nanometer**, making it impossible to see them even with a powerful microscope. It does not scatter light.
 
 
 
• **Sugar Solution**: 
 
 
• Like salt water, a **sugar solution** is also a **True Solution**. It is a **homogeneous mixture** where the solute (sugar) is uniformly distributed in the solvent (water).
 
• The particles are **molecular in size** and do not settle over time, nor can they be separated by **filtration**.
 
 
 
• **Sand in Water**: 
 
 
• This is a **Suspension**. It is a **heterogeneous mixture** containing large **solid particles** (greater than **1000 nanometers**) that are visible to the **naked eye**.
 
• If left undisturbed, the **sand particles** will settle at the bottom due to **gravity**. This mixture can be easily separated using a **filter paper**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Colloids**: Colloids are classified based on the state of the **dispersed phase** and **dispersion medium**. Common examples include **Fog** (Aerosol), **Whipped Cream** (Foam), **Jelly** (Gel), and **Muddy Water** (Sol).
 
• **Separation Techniques**: While **true solutions** cannot be separated by physical means like filtration, **colloids** like **milk** can be separated into their components (like cream/fat) using **centrifugation**.
 
• **Brownian Motion**: The particles in a **colloidal solution** move in a **zig-zag path**, known as **Brownian motion**, which helps in keeping the particles in suspension and prevents them from settling.
</ul

⇒ √200 = √(100 × 2) = 10√2

Combine the like terms:

⇒ (17√2 − 4√2)²

questions.question: P and Q together can fill a cistern with water in 10 hours. If P alone can fill the cistern with water in 20 hours, then in how many hours will Q alone fill one-fourth of the same cistern with water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity (Work) = LCM of 10 and 20 = 20 units.

Combined efficiency of (P + Q) = 20 ÷ 10 = 2 units/hr.

Efficiency of P = 20 ÷ 20 = 1 unit/hr.

Efficiency of Q = (P + Q) − P = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hr.

Time required for Q to fill 1/4 of the cistern = (20 × 1/4) ÷ 1 = 5 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipes P and Q together to fill the cistern = 10 hours

Time taken by pipe P alone to fill the cistern = 20 hours

**Method Used:**

We use the LCM method to find the total capacity of the cistern and the individual efficiency of each pipe.

 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Q = Combined Efficiency of (P + Q) − Efficiency of P

⇒ Efficiency of Q = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Total capacity of the cistern = 20 units

⇒ Work required to fill 1/4 of the cistern = 1/4 × 20 = 5 units

⇒ Time taken by Q alone = Work required ÷ Efficiency of Q

⇒ Time taken by Q = 5 ÷ 1 = 5 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 5 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns LCM Rule

Always assume the total capacity of the tank as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given individual times. This completely avoids fraction additions and simplifies efficiency calculations directly into integers.

Inlet vs Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank and is considered to be doing positive work, whereas an outlet pipe or a leak empties the tank and does negative work. Net efficiency = Sum of inlet efficiencies − Sum of outlet efficiencies.

Time and Work Equivalence

Efficiency is simply the rate of doing work per unit time. It is inversely proportional to time. Formula to remember: Total Time Taken = Total Target Work ÷ Net Efficiency.

questions.question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, angle A = 88^circ and angle B = 81^circ . The bisectors of angle C and angle D meet at O. What is the measure of angle DOC ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any quadrilateral, the angle formed by the intersection of the angle bisectors of two adjacent angles is exactly half the sum of the remaining two interior angles.

∠DOC = (∠A + ∠B) ÷ 2

∠DOC = (88° + 81°) ÷ 2

∠DOC = 169° ÷ 2

∠DOC = 84.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 84.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 A B C D O 88° 81° x x y y ? 

**Given:**

∠A = 88°

∠B = 81°

DO and CO are the angle bisectors of ∠D and ∠C respectively.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let ∠D = 2x and ∠C = 2y

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ 88° + 81° + 2y + 2x = 360°

⇒ 169° + 2(x + y) = 360°

⇒ 2(x + y) = 360° − 169°

⇒ 2(x + y) = 191°

⇒ x + y = 191° ÷ 2 = 95.5°

Now, considering the triangle ΔDOC formed by the bisectors:

⇒ ∠DOC + ∠ODC + ∠OCD = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC + x + y = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC + 95.5° = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC = 180° − 95.5°

⇒ ∠DOC = 84.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 84.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Bisectors of Opposite Angles

The acute angle formed by the intersection of the angle bisectors of two opposite angles in a non-cyclic quadrilateral is equal to half the difference of the remaining two angles. Formula: Angle = |∠B − ∠D| ÷ 2

Sum of Interior Angles

For any convex polygon with n sides, the sum of all interior angles is always given by (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral (n = 4), the sum is exactly 360°.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

If the quadrilateral is cyclic (all four vertices lie on a single circle), the sum of its opposite angles is strictly equal to 180°. Also, its exterior angle is exactly equal to the interior opposite angle.

For a 10% annual rate, the effective compound interest for 2 years is calculated using the successive percentage change formula: R + R + (R × R)/100.

Effective CI % = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%.

Total Amount = Principal (100%) + CI (21%) = 121% of Principal.

Amount = 121% of 1000 = (121/100) × 1000 = 1210.

questions.question: Why was Acko General Insurance fined ₹1 crore by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Payments to an unregistered intermediary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** imposed a significant monetary penalty of **₹1 crore** on **Acko General Insurance** in **May 2025**.
 
• The penalty was levied following a regulatory investigation that uncovered **violations related to payments made to an unregistered intermediary**. According to **IRDAI** regulations, insurance companies are prohibited from transacting or paying commissions to entities that do not hold a valid license to act as an insurance intermediary.
 
• Investigations revealed that the company had entered into arrangements where payouts were channeled to entities that were not authorized under the **IRDAI (Registration of Insurance Marketing Firms) Regulations** or the **Insurance Act, 1938**.
 
• The regulatory body observed that such practices bypass the transparent commission structures mandated for the industry and can lead to higher costs for policyholders. ***Hence, the primary reason for the fine was payments to an unregistered intermediary.***
 
• This enforcement action is part of **IRDAI's** broader mandate to maintain market discipline and ensure that all stakeholders in the insurance distribution chain are properly regulated and accountable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India):**
 
 
• It is a statutory body formed under the **IRDA Act, 1999**. It serves as the apex regulatory authority for the insurance sector in **India**.
 
• Headquartered in **Hyderabad**, its primary objectives include protecting the interests of policyholders and regulating, promoting, and ensuring the orderly growth of the insurance industry.
 
 
 
• **Acko General Insurance:**
 
 
• Founded in **2016** by **Varun Dua**, it is a prominent **Insurtech** company in **India** that follows a direct-to-consumer model.
 
• The company specializes in **digital-first** insurance products, including motor, health, and electronics insurance, often leveraging data and technology to offer competitive premiums.
 
 
 
• **Insurance Intermediaries:**
 
 
• These include agents, brokers, corporate agents, and web aggregators who act as a bridge between the insurance company and the customer.
 
• Under **Section 42** of the **Insurance Act, 1938**, no person can act as an intermediary or receive remuneration for procuring insurance business unless they are registered with the **IRDAI**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Insurance Act, 1938:** This is the cornerstone legislation for insurance in **India**. **Section 40** of this Act specifically prohibits the payment of any commission or brokerage to any person for soliciting or procuring insurance business in **India**, unless that person is an authorized agent or intermediary.
 
• **Regulatory Compliance:** **IRDAI** conducts periodic inspections and **audits** of insurance firms. Non-compliance with the **Expenses of Management (EoM)** limits or unauthorized payouts often results in stiff penalties, as seen in the **2025** ruling against **Acko**.
 
• **Solvency Ratio:** While not the reason for this specific fine, **IRDAI** mandates a minimum **solvency ratio** of **1.5 (150%)** for all insurers to ensure they have sufficient capital to settle claims even during financial stress.
 
• **Impact of Penalties:** Fines of this nature serve as a deterrent to other players in the **Insurtech** and traditional insurance space, emphasizing that digital innovation must go hand-in-hand with strict **regulatory compliance**.

• **SDSN Leadership:** The **SDSN** is currently led by **Professor Jeffrey Sachs**, a world-renowned economist and expert in sustainable development.
 
• **Data Sources:** The report relies heavily on official data from the **United Nations**, **World Bank**, **World Health Organization (WHO)**, and **International Labour Organization (ILO)**, as well as non-official data where gaps exist.
 
• **India's Context:** In the **Sustainable Development Report 2024**, **India** was ranked **109th** out of **166** countries with a score of approximately **64.0**. The country has shown progress in goals like **Climate Action** and **Responsible Consumption** but faces challenges in **Zero Hunger (Goal 2)** and **Gender Equality (Goal 5)**.
 
• **Spillover Index:** A unique feature of the **SDSN** report is the **Spillover Index**, which measures the positive and negative effects one country has on another's ability to achieve the **SDGs** (e.g., through trade, security, or environmental impacts).
